cerebro.help.title: Pad Brain
cerebro.help.intro: Pad Brain is a read-only 3D view of the local knowledge base. It represents each item as a neuron, distinguishes the type and direction of its real relationships, and shows Pad activity as pulses, without using AI tokens or writing data.
cerebro.help.first.title: First steps
cerebro.help.first.step1: Watch the cloud rotate on its own in a slow orbit.
cerebro.help.first.step2: Identify each collection by color using the legend in the corner.
cerebro.help.first.step3: Look for large nodes: these are the items with the most connections.
cerebro.help.first.stepFilters: Open the legend to filter relationships; enable ‘Hide hierarchy’ to isolate the lateral network.
cerebro.help.first.step4: Wait for or trigger real Pad activity: the neuron lights up and a particle travels along its connections.
cerebro.help.first.step5: Click a neuron to center the camera on it.
cerebro.help.first.step6: Close the window with ✕ or Esc when you finish observing.
cerebro.help.legend.title: Legend
cerebro.help.legend.neuron.name: Neuron
cerebro.help.legend.neuron.desc: a Pad item; color indicates its collection and size indicates its number of connections
cerebro.help.legend.parent.name: Hierarchy · dim gray
cerebro.help.legend.parent.desc: source → target means that the source item belongs to the target parent
cerebro.help.legend.implements.name: Implements · blue
cerebro.help.legend.implements.desc: source → target means that the source item implements the target item
cerebro.help.legend.blocks.name: Blocks · red
cerebro.help.legend.blocks.desc: source → target means that the source item blocks the target item
cerebro.help.legend.supersedes.name: Supersedes · yellow
cerebro.help.legend.supersedes.desc: source → target means that the source item supersedes the target item
cerebro.help.legend.splitFrom.name: Split from · violet
cerebro.help.legend.splitFrom.desc: source → target means that the source item was split from the target item
cerebro.help.legend.wiki.name: Wiki link · green
cerebro.help.legend.wiki.desc: source → target means that the source item's text links to the target item
cerebro.help.legend.strongPulse.name: Strong pulse
cerebro.help.legend.strongPulse.desc: a write: the item was created, updated, or commented on
cerebro.help.legend.softPulse.name: Soft pulse
cerebro.help.legend.softPulse.desc: a read performed by the console on that item
cerebro.help.legend.cluster.name: Lit cluster
cerebro.help.legend.cluster.desc: a collection-level read without a specific item
cerebro.help.legend.particle.name: Edge particle
cerebro.help.legend.particle.desc: travels from source to target in the relationship type's color when one of its nodes pulses
cerebro.help.legend.heartbeat.name: Slow heartbeat
cerebro.help.legend.heartbeat.desc: idle state: the view is alive, but there is no activity
cerebro.help.legend.live.name: Live
cerebro.help.legend.live.desc: the header confirms that the Pad is responding and the event stream is connected
cerebro.help.legend.padDown.name: Pad not responding
cerebro.help.legend.padDown.desc: the header reports that the Pad is not responding; the view preserves the drawing and retries automatically
cerebro.help.legend.reconnecting.name: Reconnecting
cerebro.help.legend.reconnecting.desc: the event stream was interrupted and the view is restoring it without losing the drawing
cerebro.help.buttons.title: Buttons and actions
cerebro.help.buttons.help.v: Opens this guide. No action in this view uses AI tokens or writes to the Pad.
cerebro.help.buttons.legend.v: Opens or closes colors and per-type filters. ‘Hide hierarchy’ removes parent links and exposes the lateral network. Uses no tokens.
cerebro.help.buttons.center.v: Centers the camera on that node. Uses no tokens.
cerebro.help.buttons.orbit.v: Rotates the view and moves the camera closer or farther away; nodes cannot be dragged. Uses no tokens.
cerebro.help.buttons.close.v: Closes the window. Uses no tokens.
cerebro.help.warning.title: Watch out for this
cerebro.help.warning.text: The Pad endpoint limits the graph to about 1,000 nodes and does not provide a way to raise that limit. If the knowledge base grows larger, the view shows a subset and does not draw edges to omitted items. The view is read-only and never writes to the Pad. The ambient heartbeat only means that the scene is alive; it does not represent activity.
